title: Repository Hermetic Target Classes
description: 🔒️ Declares which target classes run as hermetic Bazel actions: sandboxed, with exactly their declared inputs, a pinned Bun toolchain, a declared dependency tree and no network, so a sandbox or a remote executor may run them and their results are cached by content. A class selects targets by name and project, names the runtime inputs every member shares, the environment it declares as inputs and the framework ports whose host-authority implementation a hermetic one replaces. An exception removes one proven-unfit target with a closed reason, so rollout is a ratchet: widen `projects`, add an exception, never a silent host read.

Glob.description: `*` matches within one path segment, `**` across segments; every other character is literal.

Runtime.description: What every hermetic action shares: the entry module that issues the original process authority inside the action, the source patterns that module and the repository script runtime read, the files the workspace root needs.

markers.description: Workspace root files written empty when the action does not declare them, because only their presence is read.

covered.description: Runtime input commands the pinned toolchain and the execution platform already determine, so a hermetic action may drop them from its inputs.

Environment.description: Environment variables an action may declare as inputs. The value is read when the workspace is generated and enters the action manifest, so it is part of the action key and the action reads nothing else from the host.

denied.description: Prefixes that carry host authority and never enter a hermetic action.

Dependencies.description: `links` links the workspace packages the script imports by name; `packages` adds the third-party packages the project and the class name, as one content-addressed tree; `toolchain` leaves the dependencies to the toolchain of the class, which provides them as its own tree.

Toolchain.description: A toolchain a class runs on. A provisioned toolchain is a declared input of the action; an unprovisioned one keeps its members on host state under the reason `toolchain`, keyed by the pin of the toolchain, until it is provisioned. `covered` lists the runtime commands the toolchain already determines, so a member may drop them from its inputs.

Providers.description: Framework port name to the hermetic implementation module that replaces its host-authority provider inside the action; every other port keeps the repository designation.

evidence.description: `proven` ran hermetically against real targets, `derived` follows from a proven neighbour, `assumed` is declared but not yet run.

packages.description: Third-party packages the class needs besides the project's own dependencies.

Strategies.description: The spawn strategies a hermetic action may run under, by host platform: an OS sandbox where Bazel has one, otherwise the runner's own isolated root built from the declared inputs; remote execution is eligible on every host. Local unsandboxed execution is never listed because the runner refuses a root it did not isolate.
